subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — geography-weighted pool allocation
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@finlytics.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finlytics.com
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Dedicated capacity request — regional breakdown for Q3 launch

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're moving to final procurement and need a firm recommendation from Redwood on dedicated capacity sizing split by geography for our Q3 pilot and national rollouts. Key asks:

- Baseline committed pool sizes for US / EU / APAC (expected effective date: 2027-07-01)
- Burst/buffer guidance and optional burst pricing
- Any constraints for APAC provisioning and expected lead times
- PO and contracting timeline for a July start

Traffic profile: initial fanout will be ~120M tokens/month in month 1, expected to ramp to ~400M tokens/month over three months with ~60% US, 25% EU, 15% APAC token distribution. We will be serving low-latency customer-facing embeddings and chat completions (90% short-form responses). Data is regulated in EU — SOC2 + data residency is a hard requirement.

Can you send a short recommendation (numbers and assumptions) and a mutual action plan for procurement? We need this for our internal SRE and procurement review on 2027-05-10.

Thanks,
Sanjay Patel
Head of ML Platform
FinLytics

(Attachment: initial_requirements.xlsx)

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — regional breakdown for Q3 launch

Sanjay — thanks, and great to hear the timeline. Quick response for your procurement window, then we'll follow with a calc and MAP. High-level assumptions below; I'll loop infra for constraints and a detailed calc.

Assumptions (please confirm):
- Starting traffic: 120M tokens/month; ramp to 400M tokens/month over 90 days
- Model footprint: mix of 35B and 70B variants; typical latency SLO 150–250ms (p95)
- Workload: ~40% generation, 60% embeddings (embeddings are batched heavily)

Preliminary recommended committed pools (subject to infra validation):
- US: equivalent of 8 x A100-class GPUs (reserved), with 40% burst headroom
- EU: equivalent of 5 x A100-class GPUs (reserved), with 30% burst headroom
- APAC: equivalent of 4 x A100-class GPUs (reserved), with 50% burst headroom due to potential capacity constraints

I'll attach a simple template for your traffic profile (geo_capacity_template.xlsx). Marissa and Rishi — could you review the numbers and add pricing tranches + PO timelines? I will schedule an alignment call with FinLytics for tomorrow.

Happy to hop on a call to go line-by-line.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

(Attachment: geo_capacity_template.xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@finlytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — regional breakdown for Q3 launch

Looping in a quick sizing + commercial framing based on the traffic breakdown Ava outlined. I used conservative per-GPU throughput for mixed 35B/70B profiles and account for KV cache hit assumptions (30% effective token reduction on gen). Attached: capacity_calc_v2.csv.

Summary (committed pool recommendation):
- US (60% traffic): 10 reserved A100-eq GPUs — handles steady-state 240M tokens/mo with 30% buffer; suggest 2-month committed term to reduce lead time risk.
- EU (25% traffic): 4 reserved A100-eq GPUs — handles ~100M tokens/mo with 25% buffer; recommend geo-isolated pool for data residency.
- APAC (15% traffic): 3 reserved A100-eq GPUs + 2 burst slots (on-demand) — estimate steady-state 60M tokens/mo; note APAC spot availability risk, recommend 3-month commit for burst capacity or a blended reserved/burst contract.

Pricing/commercial notes:
- Tiered discount available for >$80k/mo committed spend.
- One-time onboarding credit (first-month) can be applied if PO hits by 2027-05-15.
- We can include an automatic fallback routing to higher-latency shared pools in the SOW for capacity shortfalls.

Operational asks from FinLytics: please confirm per-region peak qps (1-minute peak), % long-running sessions (if any), and whether APAC needs strict data residency (some customers require Singapore-only). Once we have that we can lock a final proposal and SOW.

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Ops — Redwood Inference
(Attachment: capacity_calc_v2.csv)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@finlytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T14:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — regional breakdown for Q3 launch

On Mon, May 2, 2027 at 08:45 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Looping in a quick sizing + commercial framing based on the traffic breakdown Ava outlined.

Thanks for the calc — a few infra points to flag before we finalize:

- APAC provisioning lead time: current partner inventory indicates 6–8 week lead time for sustained A100-equivalent reservations in Singapore. If FinLytics needs Singapore-only residency with guaranteed capacity, we should either:
  * move to a 90-day pre-commit for APAC reserved pool, or
  * accept blended model: smaller reserved pool + guaranteed burst capacity via partner (higher burst price).
- Mixed-quant option: we can save ~30% on GPU count by using 4-bit quantized variants for most of the embedding workload; need eval sign-off from FinLytics on quality tradeoffs.
- Fallback behavior: recommend routing policy that falls back from dedicated APAC -> shared APAC (higher latency) -> US/edge region (if allowed by data residency). Documented fallback needs to be part of the SOW.

Action items:
- FinLytics: confirm data residency strictness and peak qps (1-min) by 2027-05-06.
- Sales: confirm commitment window (60/90 days) for APAC reserved capacity.
- Infra: we'll draft a short risk note on inventory and expected lead times.

Jonas Weber
Head of Infrastructure — Redwood Inference

(Referenced: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-finlytics-capacity)

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — geography-weighted pool allocation

Sanjay — thanks for the quick replies and for confirming the timeline offline. To summarize and propose next steps:

- Proposed committed pools (subject to final confirmation from FinLytics on peaks and residency):
  * US: 10 reserved A100-eq GPUs
  * EU: 4 reserved A100-eq GPUs (geo-isolated)
  * APAC: 3 reserved A100-eq + 2 burst slots (partner-backed)
- We will include a mixed-quant recommendation as an optional line item in the SOW to reduce GPU count (requires eval sign-off).
- Commercial: draft SOW + MAP attached (mutual-action-plan.pdf). We're offering a first-month onboarding credit if PO is submitted by 2027-05-15.

Next steps:
1) Alignment call — propose 2027-05-04 16:00 UTC (30m) to go through the SOW and finalize PO timelines.
2) FinLytics to confirm: per-region peak qps and strictness of data residency by 2027-05-06.
3) Redwood infra (Jonas) will publish inventory risk note; Sales Ops (Marissa) to produce final pricing tranches after the call.

I'll send a calendar invite now. Looking forward to locking this down.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

(Attachment: mutual-action-plan.pdf)
